summary.intent: Set up CI/CD and Docker build changes for the API service (staging deployment workflow, Dockerfile, tsconfig build config, migrations runner) and get PR 1807 opened, reviewed, and its checks passing.
summary.outcome: Opened a draft PR (1807) touching CI workflows, the API Dockerfile, .dockerignore, tsconfig.build.json, and run-migrations.ts; configured two staging build variables; reviewed the diff, waited on CI check runs, identified failures, and pushed fixes to address review feedback and rebuild the image.

repo: apps/api has a dedicated tsconfig.build.json separate from the main tsconfig, relevant to how the Docker build compiles the API
The API Dockerfile build depends on .dockerignore contents and at least two staging-specific build variables configured outside the repo (in CI/deploy settings)
run-migrations.ts is bundled/built as part of the API image build path, not run purely from source
workflow: After pushing a PR, explicitly wait for GitHub check runs to complete and enumerate failing ones rather than assuming green CI
Before changing shared TypeScript build output (declaration files/tsconfig), check for downstream consumers of the generated .d.ts files to avoid breaking them
Use an Agent to review a PR diff for correctness/cleanup before merging, then apply fixes and re-push in a follow-up commit

friction: PR checks did not all pass on first push, requiring investigation into which check runs failed
Needed to manually verify whether other packages consume the API's generated TypeScript declaration files before finalizing tsconfig/Dockerfile changes
Docker image had to be rebuilt after applying review fixes, adding an extra iteration cycle
open_items: Confirm all previously failing check runs pass after the review-fix commit was pushed
Verify no other services still depend on the API's declaration file output in a way that the tsconfig.build.json change could break
